headline: California has banned employers from letting AI alone decide to fire or discipline a worker.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the law was signed on 30 Sep 2026 and carried in our 1 Oct edition (item 108); this is a late explainer with no new development.
importance_line: What changed: California employers of any size can no longer let AI alone decide a firing or discipline, which protects workers first and obliges employers next, but gig workers are excluded and the article gives no penalty amounts.
summary: Mashable reports that California's SB 947, the "No Robo Bosses Act", stops employers from relying only on AI or other automated tools to decide whether to fire or discipline a worker, and calls it the first law of its kind in the US. Employers must tell the worker when AI is used, and when AI is a main factor in a firing a human reviewer must back the decision with evidence such as evaluations or witness statements; Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law on 30 Sep 2026, as our 1 Oct edition reported.
notes: Older news re-dated: Mashable page dated 7 Oct 2026 says 'signed last week'; CalMatters and Bloomberg Law (our 1 Oct edition, item 108) put the signing on Wed 30 Sep 2026 and the start on 1 Jul 2027. Candidate for the 14-day duplicate check.
